summary: The root هلك (hlk) primarily means to perish or be destroyed. It can also describe a gradual perishing due to grief.
lane: 6 تَهَالَكَ غَمًّا ذ [app. He perished gradually by reason of grief. ] (A, art. سوس : see 1 in that art.) -b2- تَهَالَكَ عَلَيْهِ He was vehemently eager for it. (TA.) -b3- تَهَالَكَ فِيهِ He strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, in it, namely in running; as also . (TA.) He strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, and hastened, in it, namely an affair; as also استهلك . (TA.) -b4- تَهَالَكَتْ said of a she-camel, i. q. عَشِقَتْ [ She vehemently desired the stallion ]. (AA, TA in art. عشق .)

headwords.gloss: He; it, perished, came to nought, came to an end, passed away, was not, was no more; became non-existent

parts.t: it, perished, came to nought, came to an end, passed away, was not, was no more,
corrupt, state; became corrupted, vitiated, marred,
went away, no one knew whither:
His land had its herbage dried up by drought:

headwords.def: هَلَكَ , inf. n. هَلَاكٌ &c., (S, K, &c.,) He, or it, perished, came to nought, came to an end, passed away, was not, was no more, or became non-existent or annihilated: (KL, PS in explanation of هَلاَكٌ , &c.:) or fell: or became in a bad, or corrupt, state; became corrupted, vitiated, marred, or spoiled: or went away, no one knew whither: (Mgh in explanation of هَلاَكٌ :) he died. (K.) هَلَكَتْ أَرْضُهُ His land had its herbage dried up by drought: see جَرِبَ .

headwords.gloss: He destroyed, made an end of; caused to perish; come to an end, made away, did away with

parts.t: He destroyed, made an end of,
come to an end, made away, did away with,

headwords.def: أَهْلَكَهُ He destroyed, made an end of, or caused to perish or come to an end, made away, did away with, or brought to nought, him, or it; took away his life.

headwords.gloss: He perished gradually by reason of grief; He was vehemently eager for it; He strove, laboured, toiled

parts.t: He perished gradually by reason of grief.
He was vehemently eager for it.
exerted himself, and hastened, in it,

headwords.def: تَهَالَكَ غَمًّا [app. He perished gradually by reason of grief. ] (A, art. سوس : see 1 in that art.) تَهَالَكَ عَلَيْهِ He was vehemently eager for it. (TA.) تَهَالَكَ فِيهِ He strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, in it, namely in running; as also . (TA.) He strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, and hastened, in it, namely an affair; as also استهلك . (TA.) تَهَالَكَتْ said of a she-camel, i. q. عَشِقَتْ [ She vehemently desired the stallion ]. (AA, TA in art. عشق .)

headwords.gloss: He sought, or courted, destruction; distressed, troubled; fatigued, himself in
headwords.def: اِسْتَهْلَكَ properly signifies He sought, or courted, destruction; like اِسْتَمَاتَ : see مُسْتَمِيتَ : and see an ex. voce شَرْشَرَةٌ . اِسْتَهْلَكَ فِى كَذَا He (a man) distressed, troubled, or fatigued, himself in, or respecting, such a thing. (TA.) See also 6.

headwords.gloss: The drying up of the plants; herbage

parts.t: The drying up of the plants,

headwords.def: هَلَكَةٌ The drying up of the plants, or herbage. (AHn, TA.) See هَلاَكٌ .

headwords.gloss: Perdition; destruction; a state of perdition; destruction: a lost state; death

parts.t: Perdition; destruction; a state of perdition
He stuck fast in cases of perdition:

headwords.def: هَلاَكٌ [ Perdition; destruction; a state of perdition or destruction: a lost state; ] death. (K.) هَلاَكٌ and are syn. (S, Msb, K.) اِرْتَبَكَ فِى اِنْهَلَكَاتِ He stuck fast in cases of perdition: see art. ربك .

parts.t: as in the Kur, xxviii. last verse.

headwords.def: هَالِكٌ Dead; or dying. (Bd, Jel in xii. 85) هَالِكٌ sometimes means Subject to perish; as in the Kur, xxviii. last verse.
مَهْلِكٌ Death: see a verse cited voce سَهُوٌ .

headwords.gloss: A cause of perdition; of death; A place of perdition

parts.t: ; (S, K, TA;) because persons perish therein; (Z, TA;) or because it urges [or leads] to perdition. (TA.) See

headwords.def: مَهْلَِكَةٌ A cause of perdition, or of death. (TA in art. بخل .) (tropical:) A place of perdition or death: and a desert: (KL:) or a [ desert, or such as is termed ] مَفَازَة ; (S, K, TA;) because persons perish therein; (Z, TA;) or because it urges [or leads] to perdition. (TA.) See جَادَّةٌ .

headwords.gloss: i. q; that destroys him who seeks water, by reason of its far extent

parts.t: that destroys him who seeks water, by reason of its far extent.

headwords.def: هُوَ مُسْتَهْلِكٌ إِلَى كَذَا i. q. مُسْتَمِيتٌ [q. v.]. (TA, art. موت , from the A.) مُسْتَهْلِكُ الوِرْدِ A road that destroys him who seeks water, by reason of its far extent. (O.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
